Scattered showers will be possible tonight across the Marianas, 
particularly for Tinian and Saipan as another weak trade-wind trough
moves through the Marianas. Shower coverage is expected to become
isolated again for Thanksgiving Day, but scattered showers will 
return Thursday night as a trade-wind surge and troughing begins to 
spread across the region. Periods of scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms will persist through at least Saturday night, but model
guidance has trended downward slightly due to the upper-level 
support now being forecast to weaken. Ensemble guidance only suggests
1 to 2 inches will be possible from Thursday night through Sunday. 
Have accordingly adjusted down PoPs slightly, mostly topping out as 
low-end scattered from Thursday night through Sunday. As such, 
chances for the KBDI buster appear to be dwindling, so expect the 
KBDI to continue to slowly climb through the weekend, with today's 
value coming in at 608. This places us in the very high fire danger 
category. The aforementioned trade-wind surge will bring back higher 
east to northeast winds, from 15 to 25 miles per hour starting on 
Thursday and continuing through at least Friday. Residents are urged 
to monitor any outdoor-related activities that involve a spark or 
flames, as elevated to locally critical fire weather conditions are 
ongoing. Another, and potentially strong, trade-wind surge is 
possible starting Monday. 

Marine...
Winds and seas remain below Small Craft Advisory this afternoon, but
this is expected to be short lived as another trade-wind surge will 
increase winds back to advisory levels on Thursday. Have issued 
another Small Craft Advisory starting at noon Thursday and 
continuing through at least Friday afternoon. Model guidance 
indicates there may be a another brief reprieve Friday night and 
Saturday in advisory-level winds (sustained winds of 22 knots or 
greater and/or frequent gusts to 25 knots or greater). This surge
will also allow seas to build up to 10 feet through Friday afternoon.
Another, and potentially strong, trade-wind surge is possible
starting Monday. Otherwise, a high risk of rip currents and elevated
surf will continue through at least Friday afternoon along east-
facing reefs with a moderate risk of rip currents continuing along 
north-facing reefs. 

Eastern Micronesia...
Analysis shows seas near Arno, Majuro remaining near 9 feet, with 
altimetry showing lower seas near Kosrae. As such, we allowed the
advisories at both locations to be cancelled, while retaining
headlines. Then, the main focus continues to be on the trade winds 
that are expected to strengthen over the next few days and into the 
weekend, allowing seas and surf to build for the weekend, as the 
pressure gradient tightens. 

The models continue to show seas topping out near 11 or even 12 feet
at Majuro, 10 to 11 feet at Pohnpei, and near 9 feet at Kosrae this 
weekend. Thus, it looks like we have a 36 to 48 hour "quiet period", 
before advisories need to be hoisted once again. However, given the 
model consistency, we added/changed headlines to reflect the 
expectation of a rapid increase for seas and surf at all three 
locations (Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Majuro). As mentioned yesterday, King
Tides will only exacerbate this. As such, a minor inundation 
headline was retained at Majuro as well.

The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) remains unchanged in location from
yesterday, stretching east from near Nukuoro in the FSM (Federated
States of Micronesia) to Makin in the southern RMI (Republic of the 
Marshall Islands). Then, that pesky upper-low continues to be erratic,
with todays 6-layer ALP (All- Layer Precipitable Water) loops showing
vorticity at various levels trying to "congeal" southeast of Kosrae 
in 850-700mb layer, while 700-300mb shows it northeast of Pohnpei, 
Thus, the stretched vorticity is leading to plenty of "convective 
debris" (mid to high-level cloudiness), with scattered showers from 
earlier dissipating, per the latest infrared imagery showing rapid 
cloud top warming. However, the models remain consistent in the 
various-layered lows drifting slowly west the next few days, before 
dissipating by the weekend as high pressure to the north strengthens.
This made the forecast of who has the best rainfall potential 
somewhat challenging, but, we continued the "middle ground approach" 
from yesterday, between what the models show versus pattern 
recognition/forecaster intuition. Nevertheless, the pattern looks to 
be dominated by brisk trades at least through the weekend, with 
precipitation challenges tied to any little circulations that set up 
along the NET, or embedded areas of stronger surface convergence in 
the trade flow.

For mariners, seas remain elevated (near 9 feet) at Majuro, and
